title: JsonReconstructor.maxDepth(2) happily reconstructs eight levels
rationale: The reconstruction-side bound cannot disagree with the flattener because it is never consulted: declared, assigned, validated, and read nowhere. The repo signature pathology, and the audit history says to assume every deliverable contains one - here it is.
catchesBugClass: Dead configuration: a builder method that validates its argument, stores it, and is never read. Nothing else in this corpus can find that, because a dead control produces correct-looking output by definition.
cannotCatch: A round-trip assertion CANNOT detect this - the document round-trips exactly, so a harness checking only losslessness reports a pass and the finding disappears. It also cannot show the StackOverflow consequence, which needs thousands of levels.

predicted.detail: The document round-trips perfectly under maxDepth(2), and the probe proves the setting is inert by showing maxDepth(1) and maxDepth(1000) produce byte-identical results. Operational note: the flattener converts StackOverflowError to IllegalStateException while the reconstructor catches only Exception, so it cannot fail closed on depth.

configDescription: JsonReconstructor.builder().maxDepth(2); probe compares maxDepth(1) against maxDepth(1000) on the identical flat map

probe.note: maxDepth(1) and maxDepth(1000) must produce identical documents - that equality IS the dead-control proof, and it flips the day the setting is wired up
